evidence_basis: Graph-only neighbor of Mc3r and Bbs5; ADCY3 is a G protein effector enriched in ciliary obesity signaling.
reason: Its loss looked more like modulatory hypothalamic/ciliary GPCR output than an acute nonredundant death program in thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
counterargument: BBSome-dependent ciliary cAMP can be important in neurons, so this could be a subtype-selective signaling hit.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neighbor of Sec31a and Dock3; adhesion GPCR with synaptogenesis and spine roles.
reason: Synaptic adhesion loss was less likely to remove P16 postmitotic nuclei by P37 than direct RNA, proteasome, V-ATPase, or ER-traffic disruption.
counterargument: A sparse screen can detect identity and synaptic-state failures rather than literal cell death.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neighbor of Sec31a and Dmd; extracellular agrin receptor biology centers on NMJ and cortical synapse organization.
reason: Secreted ECM/synaptic structure did not transfer strongly to acute cell-autonomous depletion after sparse Cas9.
counterargument: Loss in neurons might disturb excitatory synapses or dystrophin-complex signaling enough to alter recovery.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Hspa9-linked mitochondrial oxidoreductase and apoptotic factor; the dossier links hypomorphic loss to progressive retinal/cerebellar degeneration.
reason: I ranked its chronic, regionally selective mitochondrial degeneration below direct Complex I assembly factors and broad essential proteostasis genes.
counterargument: AIFM1 loss can compromise respiratory-chain biogenesis and trigger apoptosis, so an acute neuronal effect is plausible.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neighbor of Eef2 and Fbxo11; ALK is a neuronal receptor tyrosine kinase tied to MAPK and PI3K signaling.
reason: Receptor signaling is modulatory and the strongest biology is gain-of-function oncology or hypothalamic energy balance, not postmitotic thalamic survival.
counterargument: Developmental or trophic RTK loss could still affect vulnerable neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Stx5a/Lrp6 neighbor with ER-cargo and collagen-turnover disease biology.
reason: I treated this as extracellular-matrix and cargo-specific traffic spillover with weak neuronal-autonomous support.
counterargument: Collagen and ER stress phenotypes mean a secretion defect could be underestimated in the frozen dossier.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Adam10/Bbs5 neighbor; FE65L1 adaptor in APP/APLP processing.
reason: APP adaptor biology was too specialized and disease evidence did not imply acute loss of thalamic glutamatergic nuclei.
counterargument: APP and ADAM10 processing can shape neuronal state, so a transcriptomic phenotype could occur.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Bbs5 neighbor; basal-body ARL2/ARL3 binder with photoreceptor and ciliary defects.
reason: The ciliary connection is real but retina/sperm-biased and less compelling than BBSome core subunits even within the rejected ciliary tier.
counterargument: Primary cilia are active signaling organelles in brain neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Psmb4/Ddx23 neighbor; ASCC3 participates in alkylation repair and stalled-ribosome quality control.
reason: Those pathways were indirect relative to the selected spliceosome, TREX, and proteasome factors, and acute postmitotic DNA repair loss need not deplete quickly.
counterargument: Ribosome quality control could intersect proteotoxic stress after guide cutting.

evidence_basis: Graph-only proteostasis neighbor; ATG5 is a core ATG12 conjugation factor and neuronal autophagy loss can cause aggregation and degeneration.
reason: Macroautophagy loss is clearly deleterious but often acts chronically, so I placed it just outside the 21-day acute P16 window.
counterargument: The visible Pomp/Psmb4 module and juvenile neurons could make autophagy loss faster than expected.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only tubular ER GTPase and ER-phagy receptor; ATL3 mutations cause sensory neuropathy.
reason: ER network maintenance was plausible but more paralog-buffered and slower than selected SEC63/COPI/COPII core transport lesions.
counterargument: A high heuristic nomination suggests the measured perturbation state may be stronger than the general biology implies.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Atp6v1a/Hspa9 graph support; SERCA2 controls ER calcium stores and SERCA inhibition triggers UPR.
reason: I selected it as an ER homeostasis hit whose calcium-store collapse should stress postmitotic neurons acutely.
counterargument: ATP2A2 disease is skin-dominant and other calcium pumps may buffer neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only but anchored to both visible V-ATPase seeds; ATP6AP1 is a membrane-sector accessory factor in V-ATPase assembly and organelle acidification.
reason: I selected it despite no heuristic nomination because loss should impair the same lysosomal and vesicular acidification axis as Atp6v1b2, Atp6v1a, Atp6v0c, and Atp6v1e1.
counterargument: Accessory status and secretory-granule specialization could make transfer weaker than catalytic subunit loss.

evidence_basis: Core V0 proton-pore gene; direct REL links to Atp6v1b2 and Atp6v1a and nine visible anchors across endomembrane/proteostasis seeds.
reason: I selected it high because acute loss should phenocopy the top V-ATPase seeds and block lysosome and synaptic-vesicle acidification.
counterargument: The c subunit sits in a multimeric V0 ring and residual protein could delay full V-ATPase collapse.

evidence_basis: Heuristic and graph candidate linked to Atp6v1b2 and Atp6v1a; ATP6V1E1 is in the V1/V0 V-ATPase assembly.
reason: I selected it high as another nonredundant V-ATPase subunit expected to compromise acidification in vulnerable neurons.
counterargument: The E subunit is not the catalytic A/B pair, so the effect might be buffered by residual complex.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Mc3r/Fbxo11 neighbor; attractin is tied to melanocortin and myelination biology.
reason: I found the pathway too specialized and partly non-cell-autonomous compared with selected essential neuronal homeostasis modules.
counterargument: Its melanocortin relationship could matter because Mc3r itself is a high visible seed.

evidence_basis: Graph-only high-multiplicity gene with OGT and ataxia links and systemic essentiality.
reason: I treated the five anchors as correlation convergence around stress modules rather than a specific acute thalamic loss-of-function mechanism.
counterargument: Systemic adult deletion can be lethal, and OGT-linked neuronal biology might transfer.

evidence_basis: B9D1 is a transition-zone ciliopathy factor with Bbs5/Nek1 and additional stress graph anchors.
reason: Primary-cilium defects were kept below the selected core trafficking and RNA-processing genes because P16-P37 loss need not remove mature thalamic neurons quickly.
counterargument: B9D1 loss compromises ciliogenesis and Hedgehog signaling, so hidden ciliary vulnerability is possible.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Brd4/Polr3b neighbor; WSTF/Baz1b acts in ISWI chromatin remodeling and DNA damage.
reason: I downweighted it because Williams-syndrome dosage and DNA-repair functions looked less acute than selected CBP, SIN3A, FACT, SETD2, and TRRAP chromatin loss.
counterargument: The broad chromatin role could still perturb neuronal transcription within the assay window.

evidence_basis: BBSome component directly related to visible Bbs5 and BBS9.
reason: It was a plausible ciliary reject, but ciliary GPCR cargo trafficking seemed slower and less lethal than selected V-ATPase or spliceosome lesions.
counterargument: Same-complex membership with Bbs5 may transfer more strongly than I allowed.

evidence_basis: BBSome core component with a graph anchor to visible Bbs5 and ciliary cargo targeting claims.
reason: I left it below the line because Bbs5 is only rank 95 and BBSome loss is more signaling/cargo selective than complete endolysosomal failure.
counterargument: Another BBSome subunit might score with a similar magnitude to Bbs5.

evidence_basis: Graph-only but directly tied to visible Polr3b; BDP1 is a TFIIIB component that recruits Pol III to promoters.
reason: I selected it because tRNA and Pol III transcription initiation are nonredundant housekeeping functions that plausibly phenocopy Polr3b loss.
counterargument: No heuristic nomination and its graph degree was low, so acute depletion might have been weaker in recovered thalamic nuclei.

evidence_basis: CAML was a graph-only high-multiplicity ER and glycosylation candidate linked to Golgi SNARE localization and neurological CDG.
reason: It narrowly missed selection because its function is less directly matched to the top visible seeds than COPI/COPII, V-ATPase, and spliceosome subunits.
counterargument: Combined glycosylation and Golgi SNARE defects make it one of the strongest rejected alternatives.

evidence_basis: Graph-only GPCR with phosphoinositide-calcium signaling and restricted brain expression.
reason: A cholecystokinin receptor is too modulatory and cell-type specific to outrank general RNA, ER, or proteasome survival genes.
counterargument: GPCR expression could mark or maintain a vulnerable thalamic subtype.

evidence_basis: Graph-only fatty-acid receptor and innate immune/microglial amyloid response gene.
reason: The dossier emphasized macrophage, microglial, and hypothalamic fatty-acid sensing more than an intrinsic thalamic glutamatergic requirement.
counterargument: Fatty-acid sensing and oxidative stress could intersect Gpx4 vulnerability.

evidence_basis: B-cell antigen receptor beta chain; graph-only Sec31a/Fbxo11 neighbor.
reason: Brain RNA absence and B-cell restriction made it a likely off-context graph artifact.
counterargument: If the screen captured rare immune contamination it could score elsewhere, but not in NeuN-positive thalamic glutamate neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Ddx23/Thoc1 neighbor; CDC40/PRP17 is required in the activated spliceosome and loss of PRP17 or PPIL1 disrupts splicing in neurodevelopmental disease models.
reason: I selected it as a direct spliceosome-function transfer from the Ddx23/Son/Tnpo3 visible module.
counterargument: It lacks a heuristic call and is a later spliceosome factor, so some splicing could persist long enough to reduce depletion.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Ddx23/Dmd neighbor; CDIN1 forms an erythroid codanin-1 complex.
reason: Erythroid differentiation and congenital dyserythropoiesis did not justify transfer to postmitotic thalamic neurons.
counterargument: Brain RNA detection leaves room for an unannotated neuronal role.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Adarb1/Atp8a2 neighbor; CELF2 regulates RNA processing and translation during neural progenitor differentiation.
reason: I ranked it below constitutive splicing/TREX factors because its best evidence is regulatory and partly developmental rather than a core spliceosome step.
counterargument: RNA-binding regulators can have sharp neuronal vulnerabilities and epilepsy links.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Pafah1b1/Eef2/Fbxo11 neighbor with CDK5/LIS1 neuronal migration biology.
reason: Postnatal loss after migration should be weaker than acute axonal motors or core tubulin turnover defects.
counterargument: CEP85L variants cause lissencephaly and epilepsy, so microtubule damage could still be harmful.

evidence_basis: Graph-only chromatin regulator tied to autism, Wnt, and fetal cortical transcription.
reason: I kept CHD8 out because the acute thalamic context favored stronger heuristic chromatin hits over developmental cortical ASD biology.
counterargument: CHD8 is a broad nonredundant chromatin remodeler and could be a hidden depletion gene.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neighbor of both V-ATPase seeds; CLCN5 is an endosomal chloride/proton exchanger.
reason: CLCN5 loss is renal and likely compensated or off-subtype in neurons compared with direct V-ATPase subunit loss.
counterargument: An endolysosomal ion imbalance might mimic V-ATPase stress if expressed in the target cells.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Pafah1b1/Fbxo11 neighbor and brain-enriched CAP-Gly microtubule linker.
reason: CLIP2 hemizygosity appears buffered in humans and its neuronal role is weaker than DYNC1H1 or KIF2A.
counterargument: The LIS1/microtubule neighborhood could contain postmigratory maintenance effects.

evidence_basis: Graph-only PTEN/Sec31a neighbor; Ras scaffold with postsynaptic and epilepsy biology.
reason: Synaptic scaffold/RAS signaling was less compelling for cell loss than core vesicle, export, splicing, or protein-turnover machinery.
counterargument: CNKSR2 loss-of-function is epileptic and alters the synaptic proteome, so neurons can be sensitive.

evidence_basis: Heuristic and graph candidate on the visible Gbf1/Sec31a/Stx5a axis; COPA is an alpha-COP coatomer subunit required for retrograde Golgi-to-ER transport.
reason: I selected it because COPI disruption should acutely perturb ER-Golgi homeostasis and SNARE/cargo recycling in the same trafficking module as top seeds.
counterargument: Heterozygous COPA syndrome is inflammatory and may not reflect acute null loss in neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only gamma-COP subunit and close COPA partner with a neurite-outgrowth paralog-specific claim.
reason: It missed the final set because no heuristic signal and COPG2/paralog buffering made it slightly less convincing than selected COPA and COPII nodes.
counterargument: It is in the same coatomer assembly as selected COPA and could deplete similarly.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neuronal palmitoyl/SAC1 regulator of AMPA receptor trafficking.
reason: SPG73 and AMPAR trafficking are neuronal but too specialized for acute depletion compared with selected cytoskeletal and ER genes.
counterargument: CPT1C is neuron-biased and could affect glutamatergic receptor handling in this class.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Brd4 graph support; CREBBP is a broad CBP acetyltransferase/coactivator required for neuronal gene programs.
reason: I selected it high because acute loss of a nonredundant transcriptional coactivator should disrupt survivor-state RNA and survival programs.
counterargument: CBP dosage disease is chronic and EP300 may buffer some acute transcription.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only centrosomal/ciliary Joubert gene.
reason: Despite heuristic support, ciliogenesis and Hedgehog developmental biology looked less acute in P16 neurons than the selected nuclear and endomembrane hits.
counterargument: The heuristic nomination could indicate a strong measured ciliary stress state in the screen.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Six3/Lrp6 Wnt candidate with beta-catenin and cadherin functions.
reason: Canonical Wnt/adhesion loss did not map as directly to this thalamic depletion phenotype as TCF7L2 itself.
counterargument: Beta-catenin is a central Wnt effector and CTNNB1 haploinsufficiency causes neurodevelopmental disease.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Eef2/Ppp2r1a neighbor; cortical upper-layer transcription factor.
reason: The available biology was cortex-developmental and morphogenetic, not a clear thalamic survival module.
counterargument: Haploinsufficiency causes human neurodevelopmental disease, so a neuronal transcriptional phenotype is plausible.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Six3/Six6 partner in SIX/EYA transcriptional biology.
reason: I treated it as developmental organogenesis or adult stem-cell biology rather than a postmitotic thalamic identity factor.
counterargument: SIX visible seeds could make a SIX/EYA/DACH module relevant.

evidence_basis: Graph-only LIS1/Fbxo11 neighbor; doublecortin acts in migration and axon outgrowth with DCLK redundancy.
reason: I downweighted it because acute P16 deletion occurs after thalamic migration and the mouse phenotype is buffered by Dclk for much of cortex.
counterargument: Neuronal microtubule stability can remain important postnatally.

evidence_basis: Heuristic and graph candidate; UAP56/DDX39B is a core helicase in the THO-TREX mRNA export machine.
reason: I selected it high because bulk nuclear mRNA export and splicing coupling should be as nonredundant as visible Thoc1.
counterargument: It was not atomically linked to Thoc1 in the frozen relations and may have partial redundancy with DDX39A.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Eef2/Ppp2r1a neighbor; DGK delta regulates DAG-to-phosphatidic acid signaling.
reason: Seizure and lipid signaling links were too indirect and nonessential compared with selected PI/ER calcium and mRNA-processing hits.
counterargument: Electrographic seizures in mutants indicate neuronal sensitivity.

evidence_basis: Graph-only but four anchors in proteostasis and ER traffic; DHDDS supplies dolichol-phosphate precursors for ER N-glycosylation.
reason: I selected it because acute loss should generate ER glycosylation stress close to the Hspa5/Gfpt1/Sec31a axis.
counterargument: Its closest dolichol-pathway partners were absent, and disease phenotypes are not thalamus-specific.

evidence_basis: Graph-only high-multiplicity RNA helicase with broad nuclear RNA-processing and ADAR-linked dsRNA functions.
reason: It was a strong reject, but its roles were regulatory and less directly mRNA-export or spliceosome-core than DDX39B, PRPF6, U2AF2, CDC40, or SNRNP70.
counterargument: DHX9 is loss-of-function constrained and neurodevelopmental, so it could have crossed the depletion line.

evidence_basis: High heuristic-only formin with actin and microtubule regulatory annotations and links to EphA4 axon retraction.
reason: I selected it at the lower end because a strong heuristic signal plus cytoskeletal remodeling could converge on Pafah1b1/Kif1a/Tbcd vulnerability.
counterargument: DIAPH2 is not a direct visible-seed graph neighbor and formin loss is not obviously lethal in postmitotic neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only mitochondrial E3 subunit shared by alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes.
reason: Respiratory metabolism matters, but this candidate lacked the heuristic and Hspa9-linked support of selected TIMMDC1.
counterargument: Neurons depend on mitochondrial oxidation and DLD deficiency can produce neurologic deterioration.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neighbor of both V-ATPase seeds with vacuolar acidification and Rabconnectin/RAVE biology.
reason: It narrowly missed because mammalian V-ATPase accessory assembly might be less directly required than ATP6AP1 and core ATP6V subunits.
counterargument: Biallelic DMXL2 loss can impair lysosomal homeostasis and cause developmental epileptic encephalopathy.

evidence_basis: Graph-only HSP40 co-chaperone and aggregate suppressor.
reason: I judged HSP70 co-chaperone specificity less likely to cause acute depletion than HSPA8 or direct proteasome loss.
counterargument: It may couple protein aggregation, HSP70, and STUB1 in neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only outer dynein arm gene enriched in motile cilia and ependyma.
reason: Motile-cilium biology is off-context for NeuN-positive thalamic glutamatergic nuclei.
counterargument: Some ciliary expression in brain-associated ependyma could confound broad graph edges, but not this class.

evidence_basis: Graph-only clathrin neighbor and dynamin vesicle-scission GTPase.
reason: Endocytic scission is relevant but DNM1 and DNM3 paralogs likely buffer neurons better than a direct CLTC/AP2 lesion.
counterargument: Dynamin loss can perturb hippocampal synapses and myopathy rescue experiments show dosage sensitivity.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neighbor of Pafah1b1 and Kif1a; DYNC1H1 is the dynein heavy chain for retrograde microtubule transport.
reason: I selected it because loss directly hits long-range axonal cargo transport, the same process suggested by visible LIS1 and Kif1a.
counterargument: Dynein knockout may be partially buffered over only three postnatal weeks or produce a state shift rather than frank depletion.

evidence_basis: Graph-only retrograde intraflagellar transport dynein-2 subunit.
reason: Primary-cilium maintenance ranked below acute core cytoplasmic transport and endomembrane failure.
counterargument: Dynein-2 loss can severely disrupt ciliary trafficking if this thalamic class depends on it.

evidence_basis: Graph-only cap-binding initiation factor downstream of PTEN/mTOR.
reason: Translation initiation looked partly regulated by paralogs and phosphorylation rather than a uniquely limiting elongation factor like visible Eef2.
counterargument: Increased EIF4E is autism-relevant, and cap-dependent translation could be dosage-sensitive.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Hspa9/Atp8a2 graph support; ELP1 scaffolds Elongator for wobble tRNA modification and neuronal codon-biased translation.
reason: I selected it because loss of tRNA modification can create proteostasis and UPR stress in neurons.
counterargument: The strongest human biology is peripheral familial dysautonomia, so thalamic glutamatergic cells may be less sensitive.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Elongator core component with neuronal proteostasis defects.
reason: It was a strong reject, but ELP1 had heuristic support and ELP2 evidence was more model- and stage-dependent.
counterargument: Same Elongator core membership could make ELP2 loss effectively equivalent to ELP1.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Eph receptor.
reason: Contact-dependent developmental/synaptic signaling was less acute and less essential than the selected modules.
counterargument: EphB signaling can regulate dendritic spines and thalamic inputs.

evidence_basis: Graph-only ERGIC cycling protein connected to the Gbf1/Sec31a ER-to-Golgi neighborhood.
reason: It missed the final set because its role is a carrier/cargo interface, weaker than coatomer and COPII coat genes.
counterargument: Biallelic ERGIC1 loss causes neurogenic arthrogryposis and may indicate neuronal sensitivity.

evidence_basis: Graph-only exocyst vesicle-tethering component.
reason: Exocytosis to plasma membrane was less tightly anchored to the visible ER-Golgi retrograde and COPII seeds than selected traffic genes.
counterargument: EXOC6B disruptions have epilepsy and developmental-delay reports.

evidence_basis: Graph-only F-box coactivator and SCF substrate receptor with motor neuropathy links.
reason: I downweighted it because F-box family membership does not imply FBXO11 or CUL3 substrate transfer.
counterargument: Some F-box perturbations may converge on neuronal proteostasis.

evidence_basis: Graph-only SCF receptor for oncogenic and Notch substrates.
reason: Loss of a tumor-suppressive substrate receptor might stabilize clients rather than acutely deplete neurons, making direction uncertain.
counterargument: NOTCH and MYC substrate accumulation could be toxic in neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only V-ATPase neighbor through FLCN/AMPK/mTOR amino-acid signaling.
reason: I treated it as nutrient-sensing regulation rather than core lysosomal acidification.
counterargument: FLCN-FNIP signaling occurs at lysosomes and could intersect V-ATPase.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Six-family developmental transcription factor not detected in adult brain atlases.
reason: Lens/ocular specificity made this a poor acute neuronal depletion candidate.
counterargument: Six3/Six6 anchoring could catch a developmental homeobox module, but FOXE3 itself looked off-context.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Wnt/PCP receptor with axon-tract developmental defects.
reason: FZD3 is important for development but receptor-level PCP signaling was not as direct as selected TCF7L2 for thalamic terminal transcription.
counterargument: Wnt receptors can affect mature neuronal morphology and might be subtype-specific.

evidence_basis: Heuristic and Gbf1/Hspa9 graph support; GFPT1 controls hexosamine entry to UDP-GlcNAc for glycosylation and its deficiency induces ER stress.
reason: I selected it as a metabolic feeder into ER protein homeostasis and OGT-linked nuclear regulation.
counterargument: Its disease and UPR evidence are muscle-heavy, and neurons may buffer HBP flux over three weeks.

evidence_basis: Graph-only 4EHP/GYF translation repression and RQC factor.
reason: Translation-coupled decay was indirect relative to EEF2/proteasome loss and lacked final-tier evidence for acute thalamic depletion.
counterargument: GIGYF2 null mice have perinatal lethality, so translation quality control can be essential.

evidence_basis: Graph-only RBX1/cullin-RING ligase inhibitor.
reason: GLMN restrains CRLs, so simple loss could increase rather than decrease ubiquitination and its human disease is vascular.
counterargument: CRL imbalance might still be toxic if the right substrates are destabilized.

evidence_basis: Graph-only cAMP transducer downstream of GPCRs.
reason: Stimulatory G protein loss is modulatory and partly isoform-buffered, not a direct counterpart of Mc3r or P2ry14 loss.
counterargument: Broad cAMP collapse can alter neuronal transcription.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Wnt and mTOR-associated kinase.
reason: GSK3A redundancy and bidirectional pathway effects made acute loss hard to map to depletion.
counterargument: GSK3B is central to beta-catenin and neuronal signaling.

evidence_basis: Graph-only TFIIH subunit connected to Taf1 and Cdk13.
reason: TTDA/GTF2H5 can have a modest steady-state transcription role and strong DNA-damage specificity, weaker than TAF1-like basal transcription loss.
counterargument: Complete mouse loss is embryonic lethal and TFIIH is part of transcription initiation.

evidence_basis: Graph-only deacetylase tied to cohesinopathy.
reason: SMC3 deacetylation and adult SVZ progenitor effects looked less direct in postmitotic neurons than selected SIN3A/CREBBP/KMT2C.
counterargument: HDAC8 is chemically tractable and loss-of-function disease shows dosage sensitivity.

evidence_basis: Graph-only large E3/GEF linked to clathrin, autophagy, mTOR, and proteasome quality control.
reason: Its biology was pleiotropic and mutation-specific, with less direct acute loss transfer than HUWE1 or VCP.
counterargument: Proteasome base quality control and neurodegeneration links could matter under Cas9 loss.

evidence_basis: Graph-only hnRNP family RBP.
reason: It was more muscle/protein-aggregation linked and less core than selected U2AF2, SNRNP70, SRRM2, CDC40, and DDX39B.
counterargument: Knockdown can alter many expression and splicing events.

evidence_basis: Graph-only RNA-processing and chromatin scaffold with cell-type-specific neuronal transcriptomic burdens.
reason: I ranked it just outside because its haploinsufficient signatures are regulatory, while selected RNA factors are constitutive splicing or export machinery.
counterargument: HNRNPU is a strong neurodevelopmental epilepsy gene and broad RBP scaffold.

evidence_basis: Graph-only RAS/MAPK candidate.
reason: HRAS and NRAS can be dispensable in mice and loss direction is opposite to many RASopathy/gain phenotypes, so it was low confidence.
counterargument: MAPK signaling is a core effector downstream of many neuronal receptors.

evidence_basis: Top heuristic plus Sec31a/Hspa9 graph support; HSPA5/BiP is the ER luminal chaperone and adaptive UPR regulator.
reason: I selected it high because ER folding capacity is nonredundant and loss should acutely engage UPR and secretory collapse.
counterargument: BiP can be stress-induced and residual protein may remain, so transcriptomic stress might be measured among survivors rather than depletion.

evidence_basis: Graph-only HSC70 central chaperone connected to ERAD, STUB1, chaperone-mediated autophagy, and clathrin uncoating.
reason: I selected it because constitutive HSP70 function links protein quality control to clathrin vesicle recycling in neurons.
counterargument: Broad chaperone systems are redundant through co-chaperones and stress inducible Hsp70s, lowering confidence.

evidence_basis: Graph-only serotonin GPCR.
reason: HTR2B is a modulatory receptor with astrocytic and cardiac-valve safety biology, not a cell-autonomous depletion factor.
counterargument: Serotonin-calcium signaling could influence specific thalamic states.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus proteasome/Trip12 graph support; HUWE1 is an E3 ligase in ubiquitination feeding proteasomal degradation and an X-linked intellectual-disability gene.
reason: I selected it because loss of a broad neuronal E3 can destabilize p53/N-Myc/proteostasis control enough for acute depletion.
counterargument: HUWE1 is a substrate-specific ligase, and developmental progenitor effects may not transfer to postmitotic thalamus.

evidence_basis: Graph-only IFT-B protein required for ciliogenesis and adult brain ciliary functions.
reason: IFT loss looked plausible but slower and more signaling-biased than the selected acute endolysosomal and vesicle traffic genes.
counterargument: Primary-cilium defects can alter adult behavior and brainwave phenotypes.

evidence_basis: Graph-only candidate with no frozen function claims.
reason: I rejected it because the visible anchors do not make an immune cytokine receptor a credible acute neuronal depletion factor, while treating absent claims as a tooling gap.
counterargument: It could have undocumented neuronal or glial signaling roles absent from the frozen dossier.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Pafah1b1/Kif1a graph support; KIF2A is a kinesin-13 microtubule depolymerase important for growth-cone microtubules and axon branching.
reason: I selected it at the cutoff as a microtubule-dynamics analog of the LIS1/KIF1A/TBCD visible module.
counterargument: Much KIF2A evidence is developmental, especially migration/axon wiring, so mature thalamic neurons may not deplete.

evidence_basis: Graph-only kinesin-2/IFT motor with ciliary and vesicle-transport functions.
reason: I ranked ciliary KIF3B below selected axonal DYNC1H1/KIF2A and below core V-ATPase trafficking genes.
counterargument: Kinesin-2 is nonredundant for IFT and could score if primary cilia are critical here.

evidence_basis: Graph-only kinesin-1 heavy chain with ALS/SPG10 and neurofilament transport evidence.
reason: It narrowly missed because KIF5 paralogs and slower axonal degeneration made it weaker than DYNC1H1 and KIF2A within a three-week assay.
counterargument: The Kif1a anchor and broad neuronal expression make it a credible hidden hit.

evidence_basis: Graph-only centrosomal/ciliary protein with retinal dystrophy biology.
reason: Spindle/photoreceptor functions were weakly relevant to postmitotic thalamic glutamatergic cells.
counterargument: Ciliary basal-body defects could cause neuronal signaling changes.

evidence_basis: Graph-only CUL3 adaptor.
reason: BTB-adaptor family membership alone was insufficient because KLHL7 substrates and retinal disease do not match visible CUL3/Fbxo11.
counterargument: Same CUL3 machinery could expose shared proteostatic stress.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only COMPASS-like H3K4 methyltransferase/coactivator causing neurodevelopmental disease.
reason: I selected it because enhancer H3K4me control should broadly alter neuronal transcription and can transfer from the Kansl1/Brd4 chromatin theme even without graph anchors.
counterargument: Heterozygous KMT2C disease is chronic and acute deletion in mature neurons may be partially tolerated.

evidence_basis: Graph-only PTEN/Adam10 synaptic scaffold.
reason: I rejected it because it modulates PTEN and receptors rather than hitting core PI3K/mTOR or survival machinery.
counterargument: PTEN recruitment and epilepsy-associated CNVs could make MAGI2 loss relevant.

evidence_basis: Graph-only ER stress modulator and BiP/IRE1-associated protein.
reason: I judged MANF more protective and modulatory than core HSPA5, SEC63, COPI, or glycosylation loss.
counterargument: Loss can increase UPR signaling, so it could sensitize stressed neurons in this screen.

evidence_basis: Graph-only central ERK kinase.
reason: Chronic ERK2 loss in forebrain glutamatergic neurons can be compensated, reducing confidence in acute depletion.
counterargument: ERK is a core effector of trophic and RAS signaling, so guide strength could matter.

evidence_basis: Graph-only kinase with brain localization.
reason: Normal Mast1-null animals and patient-like gain/missense mechanisms argued against simple acute loss depletion.
counterargument: Kinase misregulation can have sharp neuronal effects despite weak knockout evidence.

evidence_basis: Graph-only nuclear RBP linked to ALS and TREX interactions.
reason: Selective neuromuscular vulnerability and mutation-specific ALS biology were less directly relevant than the selected spliceosome/TREX factors.
counterargument: MATR3 can directly affect alternative splicing and mRNA export components.

evidence_basis: MIF is a cytokine/chemokine-like inflammatory mediator.
reason: Immune and vascular ERK signaling did not fit sparse neuronal Cas9 depletion.
counterargument: CNS inflammatory signaling may be captured indirectly in whole-brain tissue.

evidence_basis: Graph-only NOTCH-associated and adipocyte mTORC1 regulator.
reason: The dossier was pathway-diverse and not a direct match for thalamic neuronal survival.
counterargument: Parkinson-like dopaminergic abnormalities in mice suggest neuronal vulnerability.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Musashi translational regulator tied to neural progenitors and glioma.
reason: Stem-cell/progenitor enrichment and MSI2 redundancy made it unlikely to be an acute postmitotic depletion gene.
counterargument: Notch and PTEN translational control could affect neuronal states.

evidence_basis: Graph-only core mTOR kinase.
reason: Loss of MTOR or RPTOR suppresses growth signaling, whereas visible PTEN/TSC relationships involve disinhibition; direction was therefore ambiguous.
counterargument: mTOR is still a core kinase and complete loss can be deleterious.

evidence_basis: Graph-only ER lipid-transfer factor enriched in intestine and liver.
reason: ApoB lipoprotein assembly is off-context for NeuN-positive thalamic nuclei.
counterargument: It is an ER protein and secretory stress can be broadly toxic, but evidence was weak.

evidence_basis: Graph-only MYO6 actin motor in endocytosis, AMPAR traffic, and autophagosome maturation.
reason: Its roles were adaptor/cargo-specific and disease evidence favored hair cells over thalamic survival.
counterargument: Clathrin and autophagy links might transfer under acute stress.

evidence_basis: Heuristic and graph candidate; NAA15 scaffolds NatA/NatE for co-translational N-terminal acetylation of many proteins and loss causes NDD.
reason: I selected it because broad proteome acetylation defects should stress folding, stability, and proteostasis in neurons.
counterargument: N-terminal acetyltransferase loss could be slower or buffered by substrate half-lives.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus RNA/neurodevelopmental graph support; NAA20 is the catalytic NatB subunit.
reason: I selected it for a broad protein-maturation defect converging on protein stability and neuronal NDD phenotypes.
counterargument: Recessive NAA20 disease may reflect development rather than acute loss in P16 neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only BEACH/WD40 PKA-anchoring factor in post-Golgi and receptor trafficking.
reason: NBEA affects synaptic receptor sorting but is less likely to deplete nuclei acutely than core transport factors.
counterargument: NBEA variants cause neurodevelopmental epilepsy and receptor trafficking is central in glutamatergic neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Nrf1 proteasome-recovery transcription factor.
reason: I left it out because it is compensatory/upstream; loss blocks proteasome recovery but does not directly ablate the proteasome particle like PSMC1/5.
counterargument: If thalamic neurons rely on continual proteasome-gene expression, NFE2L1 loss could deplete.

evidence_basis: Graph-only oxidative-stress TF under KEAP1-CUL3 control and anchored to Gpx4.
reason: Loss of NRF2 is a loss of inducible antioxidant defense, not the catastrophic lipid-peroxidation trigger expected from direct GPX4 loss.
counterargument: It may be essential in cells under CRISPR or proteostasis stress.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only MHC class II X-box regulator with HPV/TERT literature.
reason: The available claims did not support a neuronal survival mechanism or visible-seed transfer.
counterargument: As a nuclear/RING-associated regulator it could have unreported RNA effects.

evidence_basis: Graph-only centrosomal factor active in proliferative cortical progenitors.
reason: Postmitotic P16 neurons should not depend on Ninein-mediated progenitor divisions or spindle inheritance.
counterargument: Human microcephalic dwarfism suggests developmental dosage sensitivity, but timing is mismatched.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only cohesin loader with CdLS-related cortical transcriptional programs.
reason: This was a near miss; I ranked acute postmitotic NIPBL loss below selected chromatin genes with stronger heuristic ranks and below direct graph-only core machinery.
counterargument: Cohesin loading is broad and nonredundant, so it could be a real depletion hit.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Notch receptor enriched in endothelial cells.
reason: Endothelial and vascular AVM biology is off-context for NeuN-positive thalamic neurons.
counterargument: ADAM10 anchoring points to Notch cleavage, but NOTCH4 itself looked non-neuronal.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only Gi/o neuropeptide Y receptor.
reason: I rejected it because GPCR loss is modulatory and not a direct survival gene despite possible thalamic state specificity.
counterargument: The high heuristic nomination could mark a receptor required for this TH/Prkcd/Grin2c identity state.

evidence_basis: Graph-only immediate-early nuclear receptor.
reason: Activity-dependent PV/SST and memory biology did not match an acute thalamic glutamatergic depletion mechanism.
counterargument: NR4A factors can switch neuronal transcriptional states rapidly.

evidence_basis: Graph-only vesicle ATPase connected to clathrin and V-ATPase seeds; NSF disassembles cis-SNARE complexes for vesicle traffic.
reason: I selected it at low rank because blocking the NSF/SNARE cycle should impair broad membrane traffic and synaptic release.
counterargument: NSF biology is more synaptic/recycling than survival-specific, and no heuristic nomination lowers confidence.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Dock3/Pten neighbor; TrkB trophic signaling is neuronal and survival-related.
reason: I rejected it because acute loss of one neurotrophin receptor is less directly catastrophic than selected housekeeping and trafficking lesions.
counterargument: BDNF/TrkB signaling can be required by specific neurons, so this may be a false negative call.

evidence_basis: Graph-only clathrin/PTEN phosphatase with PI(4,5)P2 endosomal functions.
reason: Mouse Ocrl loss is paralog-buffered by Inpp5b, weakening acute single-gene transfer.
counterargument: Phosphoinositide imbalance can strongly perturb endocytosis and Golgi trafficking.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus nuclear-transport graph support; OGT O-GlcNAcylates many nuclear and cytoplasmic proteins, including nucleoporins, and affects adult neuronal physiology.
reason: I selected it because loss of global O-GlcNAc cycling should perturb nuclear transport, transcription, and protein homeostasis.
counterargument: UDP-GlcNAc/O-GlcNAc pathways are broad and may alter state without causing preferential thalamic depletion.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Six3/Six6 homeobox factor.
reason: Adult OTX2 is largely choroid-plexus sourced and acts non-cell-autonomously in PV-lineage cells, making direct thalamic glutamatergic transfer weak.
counterargument: Developmental homeobox activity can define regional identity, so residual expression might matter.

evidence_basis: B-lineage transcription factor with B-cell expression.
reason: I rejected it as an off-context graph artifact for NeuN-enriched thalamic neurons.
counterargument: Embryonic midbrain-hindbrain roles exist, but timing and lineage do not match.

evidence_basis: Graph-only RTK/pericyte candidate linked to vascular calcification.
reason: Pericyte and smooth-muscle expression made it inappropriate for sorted neuronal nuclei.
counterargument: PDGFRB/XPR1 phosphate-calcification biology could perturb thalamic tissue non-cell-autonomously, but sparse neuronal guides should not target pericytes.

evidence_basis: Graph-only phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase associated with clathrin, Psmb4, and Pten.
reason: PI4K activity is broad but the available support was not as direct as selected COPI/COPII/ESCRT genes.
counterargument: Phosphoinositide supply controls endomembrane traffic and could be acutely limiting.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Golgi PI4K connected to Gbf1 and Pten.
reason: I rejected it because a regulated lipid kinase was less directly matched to visible Gbf1/Stx5a than COPI/COPII structural genes.
counterargument: Golgi PI4P is central to trafficking, so single-gene loss could stress neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Eef2/Fbxo11 neighbor and membrane contact/lipid transfer factor.
reason: The function is too indirect and not anchored to top visible seeds with atomic support.
counterargument: Lipid exchange at contacts can modulate ER/Golgi and plasma-membrane homeostasis.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only calcineurin regulatory subunit.
reason: Calcineurin signaling is activity-modulatory and less plausibly depletes nuclei than the selected housekeeping hits.
counterargument: PPP3CA pathogenic variants show that this phosphatase pathway matters in neurodevelopment.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Ddx23/Son/Tnpo3 graph support; PRPF6 is required for stable U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP spliceosome assembly and directly linked to visible Ddx23.
reason: I selected it at the top because acute loss should globally disrupt pre-mRNA splicing in the same machinery as Ddx23 and SON-associated nuclear speckles.
counterargument: Some PRPF6 disease is retinal despite ubiquitous expression, so not every neuron is equally sensitive.

evidence_basis: Heuristic and highest graph multiplicity; PSMC1 is a 19S AAA ATPase and conditional mouse neuron loss depletes 26S proteasomes and causes neurodegeneration.
reason: I selected it because it directly phenocopies the visible Psmb4/Pomp proteasome axis and should be nonredundant.
counterargument: Heterozygosity is buffered in whole mouse brain, so guide efficiency and residual ATPase levels could tune the effect.

evidence_basis: Heuristic and graph candidate; PSMC5 is a 19S proteasome-base ATPase related to PSMC1 and anchored to visible Psmb4/Pomp.
reason: I ranked it first because loss of a proteasome AAA ATPase should acutely collapse ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation and activate lethal proteotoxic stress.
counterargument: Some PSMC5 evidence is from non-neuronal apoptosis assays, and it may not be stronger than PSMC1 in thalamic neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only PPP2R1A/PTEN neighbor and PP2A activator.
reason: PP2A activation was indirect and not an obvious acute depletion mechanism compared with PPP2R1A scaffold loss.
counterargument: Phosphatase regulation could affect survival signaling broadly.

evidence_basis: Graph-only PPP2R1A/PTEN neighbor; likely ER stress and transcriptional response factor.
reason: No direct inspected dossier was needed because nomination support was weak and it lacked a visible-seed module match.
counterargument: QRICH1 can shape ER stress transcription and could intersect HSPA5.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Rab with photoreceptor outer-segment loss-of-function disease.
reason: Retinal ciliary trafficking was too specialized for thalamic neurons.
counterargument: BBS5/Nek1 anchoring might reflect a primary-cilium module.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus broad graph support; RANBP2 is a nuclear-pore cytoplasmic filament factor and SUMO E3 linked to export-complex disassembly.
reason: I selected it because nuclear pore and SUMOylation defects should stress RNA/protein transport in concert with Tpr, Thoc2, and Xpo1.
counterargument: RanBP2 is peripheral and not a direct TREX or spliceosome subunit, making exact transfer uncertain.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Six3/Six6/Fbxo11 homeobox factor.
reason: Retina, pituitary, and hypothalamic developmental claims did not fit postnatal thalamic depletion.
counterargument: Its Six3/Six6 links and homeobox identity could signal a real regional module.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only tumor suppressor whose neuronal loss can trigger ectopic S-phase entry and neuronal loss.
reason: I selected it as a low-confidence but plausible acute postmitotic cell-cycle re-entry lesion.
counterargument: Rb family compensation and context-dependent knockout phenotypes make the loss direction uncertain.

evidence_basis: Graph-only FIP200/ULK autophagy initiation scaffold with four anchors.
reason: I ranked it below selected core ER/Golgi and proteasome genes because autophagy initiation is slower and mTOR-regulated.
counterargument: FIP200 is core to autophagosome formation and could be more acute in stressed neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only extracellular RELN ligand.
reason: Secreted Reelin signaling has strong developmental migration roles but weak acute cell-autonomous loss-of-function transfer.
counterargument: Reelin can affect mature synapses and epilepsy, so state effects are possible.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neuronal-gene repressor connected to SIN3A.
reason: REST loss direction is not simply toxic in neurons and may derepress neuronal programs rather than deplete them.
counterargument: REST can be neuroprotective or pro-death depending on stress context.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus graph candidate; RNPC3 is the U11/U12-65K factor in minor intron splicing.
reason: I selected it because minor-spliceosome failure can still broadly disrupt long neuronal transcripts and mapped near Ddx23/Cdk13.
counterargument: Human disease is surprisingly endocrine-restricted for a core RNA-processing factor.

evidence_basis: Graph-only connecting-cilium gene strongly biased to photoreceptor disease.
reason: Its ocular gene-therapy and retinal evidence was far from thalamic glutamatergic survival.
counterargument: General ciliary trafficking defects could still matter in neurons but RPGR looked specialized.

evidence_basis: Graph-only mTORC1 scaffold.
reason: Like MTOR, loss of the active mTORC1 arm has ambiguous direction relative to PTEN/TSC suppressor-loss disease.
counterargument: mTORC1 can be required for neuronal growth and metabolism.

evidence_basis: Graph-only AP-4 accessory factor linking ATG9A vesicles to kinesin.
reason: AP-4/ATG9A traffic was plausible but more selective than selected DYNC1H1, V-ATPase, and COPII hits.
counterargument: RUSC2 loss causes microcephaly and severe intellectual disability, so neurons may be sensitive.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only sacsin loss causes ARSACS and Purkinje-cell degeneration.
reason: I rejected it because its loss is chronic and regionally selective rather than an acute broad thalamic survival defect.
counterargument: Mitochondrial and neurofilament collapse in long neurons could emerge within weeks.

evidence_basis: Graph-only COPII initiating GTPase connected to Gbf1, Sec31a, and Stx5a.
reason: It narrowly missed because SAR1A paralogy and chylomicron-retention disease imply cargo and paralog context, whereas SEC23A and COPA were stronger.
counterargument: SAR1B is directly upstream of SEC23/24 recruitment and could still phenocopy Sec31a.

evidence_basis: Graph-only COPII inner-coat factor directly connected to Sec31a.
reason: I selected it because COPII vesicle biogenesis should perturb ER export on the same axis as visible Sec31a and Gbf1.
counterargument: SEC23A and SEC23B can be interchangeable in vivo, so paralog buffering may reduce acute depletion.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only ER membrane auxiliary factor for SEC61/BiP protein translocation and folding.
reason: I selected it because failure of ER import should create proteostasis stress closely related to HSPA5 and the secretory-traffic module.
counterargument: SEC63 disease evidence is kidney/liver and may involve specific secretory cargo.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only Pol II-associated H3K36 trimethyltransferase with links to transcriptional chromatin and neuronal gene expression.
reason: I selected it because H3K36me3 loss can disturb transcription elongation, splicing, and neuronal protocadherin programs.
counterargument: Developmental cortical claims may not transfer to mature thalamic neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only RNA:DNA helicase for R-loop resolution and Pol II termination.
reason: SETX was less direct to the acute spliceosome/TREX axis and has divergent gain- and loss-of-function disease mechanisms.
counterargument: R-loop accumulation can damage long neuronal genes and could become toxic after Cas9.

evidence_basis: Graph-only sarcoglycan associated with myoclonus-dystonia.
reason: Dystrophin-complex membership with Dmd was not enough; Sgce mutant striatum can show nearly normal RNA-seq markers.
counterargument: Synaptic LTD and dopamine defects could create cell-state vulnerability.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only HDAC scaffold; SIN3A haploinsufficiency causes intellectual disability and has postnatal hippocampal excitatory-neuron roles.
reason: I selected it because a broad nonredundant chromatin corepressor should perturb gene expression enough for acute depletion or identity loss.
counterargument: Corepressor loss can derepress rather than disable transcription and was not graph-anchored.

evidence_basis: Six-family graph neighbor of Six3 and Six6 but largely embryonic and not broadly detected in adult brain.
reason: I rejected it as a weak family transfer without adult thalamic support.
counterargument: Six-family factors are exactly visible seeds, so any hidden thalamic SIX expression could matter.

evidence_basis: Graph-only SIX family transcription factor with ocular and BOR syndrome links.
reason: SIX5 looked less brain- and thalamus-relevant than Six3/Six6 and lacked heuristic support.
counterargument: SIX/EYA family redundancy could hide a related role.

evidence_basis: Graph-only bicarbonate transporter anchored to both V-ATPase seeds.
reason: Plasma-membrane pH regulation was not as central as organellar V-ATPase acidification and had weaker depletion plausibility.
counterargument: Neuronal pH homeostasis can alter excitability and survival.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Psmb4/Son/Ddx23 neighbor with progressive myoclonic epilepsy loss-of-function evidence but little mechanistic specificity.
reason: I rejected it because the dossier lacked a direct function tying it to RNA or proteasome transfer.
counterargument: The human epilepsy phenotype could indicate a real neuronal survival pathway.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only SLF1/RAD18/SMC5/6 genome-stability factor for replication-associated damage.
reason: Stalled-replication-fork biology is mismatched to postmitotic neurons except after genotoxic stress.
counterargument: Cas9 cutting might create enough DNA repair burden to expose SLF2 loss.

evidence_basis: Graph-only BMP receptor SMAD.
reason: The PV-interneuron activity evidence and BMP signaling were off-target for thalamic glutamatergic depletion.
counterargument: BMP-SMAD transcription can be activity-regulated in adult neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only chromatin remodeler with heterochromatin and DNA-break roles.
reason: The disease signal was skin-specific and DNA-repair functions were weaker than selected transcriptional chromatin genes.
counterargument: Double-strand break repair after Cas9 could make chromatin repair genes score.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Smoothened Hedgehog transducer.
reason: Hedgehog signaling is developmental and receptor-transducer loss lacks direct postmitotic thalamic survival evidence.
counterargument: Primary-cilium Hedgehog defects might converge with BBS/Nek1 signals.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neuronal SNARE needed for transmitter release and linked to early epileptic encephalopathy.
reason: I left it out because blocking evoked exocytosis is not necessarily cell-lethal in isolated mosaic neurons.
counterargument: Broad synaptic vesicle fusion failure could cause rapid maladaptive transcription or loss of recovered nuclei.

evidence_basis: Graph-only U1 snRNP factor connected to Son, Thoc1, Psmb4, and Pomp.
reason: I selected it because U1 snRNP loss should compromise splice-site recognition, a direct essential RNA-processing step.
counterargument: It lacks a heuristic nomination and the dossier was less explicit about acute neuronal loss than PRPF6 or CDC40.

evidence_basis: Graph-only SOX factor enriched in endothelial lymphangiogenesis.
reason: Endothelial expression and Sox7/Sox17 compensation made it off-context and buffered.
counterargument: Sox17 was a visible seed, but same-family membership was insufficient here.

evidence_basis: Graph-only SOXB1 developmental factor with selected adult brain abnormalities.
reason: It was plausible but mostly progenitor/maintenance biology and no thalamic identity evidence comparable to TCF7L2.
counterargument: Sox2 deficiency can affect adult thalamus, so it could be a hidden transcriptional hit.

evidence_basis: Graph-only but atomically connected to SON; SRRM2 is a nonredundant nuclear-speckle and splicing-condensate scaffold.
reason: I selected it because the visible SON/Tnpo3/Ddx23 axis points to nuclear speckles and mRNA processing, and SRRM2 loss should disrupt that architecture.
counterargument: It was not heuristic-nominated, and speckle remodeling may change splicing state more than survival.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Son/Tnpo3/Ddx23 graph support; SRSF1 is an SR splicing factor and TNPO3 cargo with human loss-of-function NDD evidence.
reason: I selected it high because loss hits both alternative splicing and the visible SR-protein nuclear-import module.
counterargument: Some SRSF paralogs may buffer subsets of splicing targets.

evidence_basis: Graph-only CHIP chaperone-coupled ubiquitin ligase.
reason: STUB1 is important in proteostasis but is adaptor-specific and not as direct as selected VCP/HSPA8/proteasome hits.
counterargument: CHIP connects HSP70 clients to the proteasome and could be limiting under stress.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Munc18-1 SNARE release factor with four anchors.
reason: Despite a severe epilepsy disease gene, neurotransmitter release loss in sparse mosaic neurons may silence cells without killing them.
counterargument: STXBP1 is core synaptic fusion machinery and could affect recovery or neuronal identity.

evidence_basis: High heuristic plus Kansl1/Psmb4/Pomp graph support; SPT16 is linked to SSRP1 and transcription-elongation factors.
reason: I selected it because FACT-dependent nucleosome reorganization is a broad transcriptional requirement likely to stress postmitotic nuclei.
counterargument: The frozen dossier lacked a strong direct neuronal loss claim and even noted weaker proteasome similarity.

evidence_basis: Graph-only synaptic-vesicle phosphoprotein.
reason: Synaptic vesicle reserve-pool regulation is too specialized and nonlethal for acute depletion.
counterargument: Synaptic vesicle defects could alter glutamatergic activity states.

evidence_basis: Graph-only nuclear-envelope cytoskeletal linker.
reason: Chronic ataxia/nuclear positioning biology was less direct than nuclear pore/export genes Tpr, Ranbp2, and Xpo1.
counterargument: Neurons with long processes can be sensitive to nuclear-cytoskeletal defects.

evidence_basis: Graph-only phosphoinositide phosphatase in synaptic-vesicle endocytosis.
reason: Synaptic endocytosis was downranked for the same reason as DNM2 and SNAP25: strong function, weak survival transfer.
counterargument: Parkinsonism and clathrin-linked vesicle recycling could become toxic in mature neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only ALS-linked RBP.
reason: TDP-43 disease is mostly toxic gain/mislocalization and downstream splicing, not simple acute loss in thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
counterargument: Loss of nuclear TDP-43 function is pathogenic in ALS and could affect long neuronal transcripts.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Six3/Lrp6 graph support; TCF7L2 regulates postmitotic thalamic differentiation and electrophysiological gene programs in mice.
reason: I selected it at the cutoff because it is the most thalamus-specific developmental transcription factor in the pool.
counterargument: It may control identity rather than survival and had a low heuristic rank.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Atp6v1a/Ank3 neighbor and TFCP2-family factor.
reason: TFCP2 family redundancy and lack of neuronal survival evidence made it weak.
counterargument: General transcription-factor loss can have unexpected subtype effects.

evidence_basis: Top heuristic-only gene in the same THO-TREX mRNA export complex as visible Thoc1 and selected Ddx39b.
reason: I selected it high because failed mature mRNA export, R-loop accumulation, and DNA damage should acutely threaten postmitotic neurons.
counterargument: It was not graph-nominated despite the obvious THOC1 relationship, indicating the comparator signature may differ.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only inner-mitochondrial Complex I assembly factor whose depletion reduces respiration and whose biallelic variants cause neurologic Complex I deficiency.
reason: I selected it because respiratory-chain assembly loss can directly starve vulnerable neurons and mirrors the visible Hspa9 mitochondrial chaperone theme.
counterargument: Complex I turnover may be slow enough that a P16-P37 screen captures state changes before depletion.

evidence_basis: Graph-only glutamatergic fate TF in embryonic dorsal spinal cord.
reason: Wrong developmental region and timing made it a weak transfer to thalamic postmitotic neurons.
counterargument: Its glutamatergic fate role means it could alter identity if unexpectedly expressed.

evidence_basis: Graph-only membrane protein linked to APP and gamma-secretase/Notch in flies.
reason: The mechanism is poorly direct and not specific to the selected ADAM10/Notch axis.
counterargument: Notch cleavage biology could intersect Adam10 seed function.

evidence_basis: Graph-only Complex I assembly factor.
reason: It was plausible but ranked below heuristic TIMMDC1 within the same pathway and below stronger direct graph modules.
counterargument: TMEM126A loss can impair ND4-module assembly and oxidative phosphorylation.

evidence_basis: Graph-only lysosomal zinc transporter.
reason: I treated it as a specialized lysosomal ion transporter with oligodendrocyte/myelin disease rather than broad V-ATPase-like acidification.
counterargument: Lysosomal zinc handling can intersect endolysosomal stress.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Tnpo3/Thoc1 graph support; TPR is a nuclear-basket factor in mRNA export and TREX-2-linked RNA export.
reason: I selected it high because nuclear pore mRNA export loss transfers strongly from the visible THOC/TNPO3 RNA-processing module.
counterargument: TPR preferentially affects short intron-poor genes and may not mimic spliceosome failure.

evidence_basis: Graph-only mitochondrial and GABA-A/endosomal trafficking adaptor.
reason: I rejected it because RHOT/KIF5 mitochondrial transport is cargo-specific and slower than selected DYNC1H1 core dynein loss.
counterargument: TRAK1 variants cause severe developmental epileptic encephalopathy.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus Kansl1/Brd4 graph support; TRRAP is a scaffold of NuA4 and SAGA HAT complexes.
reason: I selected it because losing a general HAT scaffold should broadly compromise chromatin coactivation in neurons.
counterargument: Most strong data involve progenitor cell-cycle gene transcription, not acute postmitotic neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only TSC complex component with neuronal mouse loss causing mTOR activation, seizures, dysplasia, and limited survival.
reason: I left it out because TSC1 loss activates growth signaling rather than removing a housekeeping process, and PTEN itself was a low visible seed.
counterargument: TSC1 had multiple anchors and strong neuronal mouse phenotypes, making it a serious near-cutoff alternative.

evidence_basis: Graph-only TSC complex GAP component upstream of mTORC1.
reason: I downweighted it with TSC1 because suppressor loss and mTOR hyperactivation need not mimic acute depletion in this thalamic class.
counterargument: Same TSC complex membership and four anchors could mean TSC2 is just below true detection.

evidence_basis: Tetraspanin Norrin/FZD4/LRP5/6 co-receptor active in retinal endothelial/barrier biology.
reason: Wnt co-receptor function is vascular and FZD4-specific, not a thalamic neuronal Wnt effector.
counterargument: Blood-brain barrier Wnt pathways can indirectly affect neurons but sparse neuronal CRISPR makes that unlikely.

evidence_basis: Graph-only tetraspanin affecting AMPAR trafficking and dendritic spines.
reason: Synaptic receptor trafficking looked sublethal relative to the selected core transport genes.
counterargument: X-linked intellectual disability and hippocampal rescue experiments support real neuronal dosage effects.

evidence_basis: Tubulin glutamylase linked mostly to photoreceptor connecting cilia and sperm axonemes.
reason: The relevant disease and expression context was too retina/testis-skewed.
counterargument: Tubulin post-translational modification may affect neuronal microtubules broadly.

evidence_basis: Graph-only neuronal beta-tubulin isotype.
reason: Long-term Tubb3 null is largely compensated by other beta-tubulins, so simple loss looked buffered.
counterargument: Missense TUBB3 disease shows that this isotype can perturb neuronal microtubule dynamics.

evidence_basis: Graph-only but connected to Psmb4, Son, Pomp, Ddx23, and Thoc1; U2AF2 is a core splice-site factor.
reason: I selected it because U2AF2 loss should directly impair pre-mRNA splicing and fits the visible Ddx23/Son RNA-processing theme.
counterargument: It was not heuristic-nominated and the dossier emphasized NDD association more than acute neuronal depletion.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only UFM1 E1 enzyme.
reason: I selected it because UFMylation is an ER/protein-homeostasis ubiquitin-like pathway and biallelic loss causes severe early-onset encephalopathy.
counterargument: UFMylation is not the same pathway as 26S ubiquitination, and acute postmitotic transfer is uncertain.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only N-end-rule E3 ligase.
reason: I selected it because it feeds ubiquitin-proteasome degradation and had a strong enough heuristic rank to keep above graph-only substrate-specific E3s.
counterargument: UBR1 human disease is Johanson-Blizzard syndrome and single E3 loss may be substrate-selective.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only Munc13 presynaptic vesicle-priming factor.
reason: I rejected it because presynaptic priming failure is more likely to silence or change firing than to remove thalamic nuclei in a sparse mosaic.
counterargument: Seizure genetics and the heuristic rank make it a plausible hidden synaptic candidate.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only deubiquitinase tied to neurodevelopment and Wnt/Notch/TGF-beta pathways.
reason: It was a near miss but ranked below UBR1/HUWE1 because its substrate network is less directly proteasomal and more developmental.
counterargument: Female USP9X loss-of-function and mouse forebrain phenotypes show strong neuronal dosage sensitivity.

evidence_basis: Graph-only ER FFAT-binding contact-site scaffold with ALS8 links.
reason: ER contacts and mutant aggregation biology were less direct than selected SEC63, HSPA5, and COPII/COPI defects.
counterargument: ER-mitochondrial contact loss can perturb calcium and UPR homeostasis.

evidence_basis: Graph-only proteostasis segregase anchored to Psmb4, Pomp, and Nek1.
reason: I selected it because VCP extracts ubiquitylated substrates for proteasomal and ERAD handling, so loss should generate proteotoxic and ER stress close to the PSMC/Psmb4 module.
counterargument: VCP disease mutants can be gain or altered function, and VCP is upstream of multiple pathways rather than the proteasome core.

evidence_basis: Graph-only with six anchors including Chmp4b and Snf8; VPS37A is an ESCRT-I factor required for multivesicular-body sorting and lysosomal degradation.
reason: I selected it because loss transfers well from the visible ESCRT genes Chmp4b and Snf8 and should block endolysosomal cargo disposal.
counterargument: ESCRT-I is upstream of CHMP4B, and the proteasome anchors may be indirect.

evidence_basis: Graph-only GARP/EARP subunit with endosome-to-TGN retrieval and cerebello-cerebral atrophy evidence.
reason: I kept it just outside because GARP retrieval is slightly more indirect than selected ESCRT/V-ATPase/COPI/COPII lesions.
counterargument: VPS53 and visible traffic genes converge on lysosomal enzyme sorting and SNARE-complex assembly.

evidence_basis: GARP-complex retrograde factor with the mouse wobbler motor-neuron phenotype.
reason: Low graph degree and partial-loss motor neuron specificity made it weaker than VPS53 and selected traffic genes.
counterargument: GARP loss can destabilize retrograde traffic and cause neurodegeneration.

evidence_basis: Heuristic plus graph candidate; WAC links Pol II to RNF20/RNF40 H2B ubiquitination and WAC loss-of-function causes NDD.
reason: I selected it at the cutoff because broad transcription-coupled H2B ubiquitination could transfer from the chromatin/RNA processing seeds.
counterargument: WAC is not same-complex with the visible anchors and may be a slower developmental dosage gene.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only WASH complex subunit in endosomal Arp2/3 regulation.
reason: It was plausible but weaker than ESCRT and V-ATPase/GARP traffic genes for acute thalamic depletion.
counterargument: WASHC4 disruption causes neuronal endolysosomal changes, so it is a real near-cutoff alternative.

evidence_basis: High-multiplicity graph-only CTLH E3 subunit with haploinsufficient NDD and seizures.
reason: I treated the eight anchors as broad stress convergence rather than direct same-complex transfer, leaving it below UBR1/HUWE1/VCP.
counterargument: High graph degree and ubiquitin-ligase function make this a notable possible miss.

evidence_basis: Graph-only inhibitor of apoptosis and NOD2 signaling gene.
reason: XIAP loss relieves caspase inhibition but human disease is immune dysregulation, making neuronal loss uncertain.
counterargument: It can gate cytochrome-c-dependent caspase activation in neurons under stress.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only exportin-1 for broad protein and RNP nuclear export.
reason: I selected it because nuclear export failure should pair with selected Tpr/Ranbp2/TREX mRNA-export lesions and compromise mature neurons.
counterargument: XPO1 inhibition is reversible pharmacology and its RNA-processing links are indirect.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only SLC53A1 phosphate exporter with basal-ganglia calcification disease biology and thalamic involvement in heterozygous mice.
reason: I selected it because phosphate efflux can be nonredundant and the high heuristic rank suggested a strong stress state despite no graph anchors.
counterargument: Its chronic disease may be vascular/astrocytic rather than cell-autonomous in thalamic glutamatergic neurons.

evidence_basis: Graph-only cytoplasmic 5-3 exoribonuclease linked to Cnot1.
reason: mRNA decay was plausible but less direct than selected nuclear splicing/export factors and lacked heuristic support.
counterargument: Forebrain Xrn1 conditional knockout causes brain metabolic phenotypes, so mRNA decay can be neuronal.

evidence_basis: Graph-only ATAC complex reader linked to Brd4/Kansl1.
reason: It was less direct than TRRAP within HAT complex biology and lacked neurodevelopmental loss-of-function evidence as strong as CREBBP/KMT2C.
counterargument: ATAC chromatin programs can be broadly required.

evidence_basis: Heuristic-only predicted KRAB C2H2 transcription factor.
reason: The dossier had only generic DNA-binding annotation and no neuronal or seed-module evidence.
